stoker: 1. One who is employed to tend a furnace and supply it with fuel, especially the furnace of a locomotive or of a marine steam boiler; also, a machine for feeding fuel to a fire. 2. A fire poker. C. Richardson (Dict.).
steatopygous: Having fat buttocks. Specimens of the steatopygous Abyssinian breed. Burton.
straitness: The quality or condition of being strait; especially, a pinched condition or situation caused by poverty; as, the straitnessof their circumstances.
storify: To form or tell stories of; to narrate or describe in a story. (old)
strophiolated: Furnished with a strophiole, or caruncle, or that which resembles it. Gray.
stalworthhood: The quality or state of being stalworth; stalwartness; boldness; daring. (old)
stereoscopical: Of or pertaining to the stereoscope; characteristic of, or adapted to, the stereoscope; as, a stereoscopic effect; the stereoscopic function of the eyeglasses; stereoscopic views. -- Ste`re*o*scop"ic*al*ly, adv.
stylops: A genus of minute insects parasitic, in their larval state, on bees and wasps. It is the typical genus of the group Strepsiptera, formerly considered a distinct order, but now generally referred to the Coleoptera. See Strepsiptera.
stalactite: (a) A pendent cone or cylinder of calcium carbonate resembling an icicle in form and mode of attachment. Stalactites are found depending from the roof or sides of caverns, and are produced by deposition from waters which have percolated through, and partially dissolved, the overlying limestone rocks. (b) In an extended sense, any mineral or rock of similar form and origin;
storm: 1. steelbowgoods: Those goods on a farm, such as corn, cattle, implements husbandry, etc., which may not be carried off by a removing tenant, as being the property of the landlord.
stillsonwrench: A pipe wrench having an adjustable L-shaped jaw piece sliding in a sleeve that is pivoted to, and loosely embraces, the handle. Pressure on the handle increases the grip.
sturt: To vex; to annoy; to startle. [Obs. or Prov. Eng. & Scot.] | 1. Disturbance; annoyance; care. [Obs. or Prov. Eng. & Scot.] "Sturt and care." J. Rolland. 2. (Mining) A bargain in tribute mining by which the tributor profits. Raymond.
stonerunner: (a) The ring plover, or the ringed dotterel. [Prov. Eng.] (b) The dotterel. [Prov. Eng.]
stenosis: A narrowing of the opening or hollow of any passage, tube, or orifice; as, stenosis of the pylorus. It differs from stricture in being applied especially to diffused rather than localized contractions, and in always indicating an origin organic and not spasmodic.
streaked: 1. Marked or variegated with stripes. 2. Uncomfortable; out of sorts. [Local, U.S.]
strophiole: A crestlike excrescence about the hilum of certain seeds; a caruncle.
starry: 1. Abounding with stars; adorned with stars. "Above the starry sky." Pope. 2. Consisting of, or proceeding from, the stars; stellar; stellary; as, starry light; starry flame. stibiconite: A native oxide of antimony occurring in masses of a yellow color.
strenuous: Eagerly pressing or urgent; zealous; ardent; earnest; bold; valiant; intrepid; as, a strenuous advocate for national rights; a strenuous reformer; a strenuous defender of his country. And spirit-stirring wine, that strenuous makes. Chapman. Strenuous, continuous labor is pain. I. Taylor. -- Stren"u*ous*ly, adv. -- Stren"u*ous*ness, n.
strongminded: Having a vigorous mind; esp., having or affecting masculine qualities of mind; -- said of women. -- Strong"-mind`ed*ness, n.
stockman: A herdsman; a ranchman; one owning, or having charge of, herds of live stock. [Australia & U.S.] W. Howitt.
stipend: Settled pay or compensation for services, whether paid daily, monthly, or annually.
stakehead: A horizontal bar on a stake, used for supporting the yarns which are kept apart by pins in the bar.
strude: A stock of breeding mares. [Written also strode.] (old) Bailey.
steaminess: The quality or condition of being steamy; vaporousness; mistness.
stonehatch: The ring plover, or dotterel. [Prov. Eng.]
stint: (a) Any one of several species of small sandpipers, as the sanderling of Europe and America, the dunlin, the little stint of India (Tringa minuta), etc. Called also pume. (b) A phalarope. | 1. stringcourse: A horizontal band in a building, forming a part of the design, whether molded, projecting, or carved, or in any way distinguished from the rest of the work.
steeling: The process of pointing, edging, or overlaying with steel; specifically, acierage. See Steel, v.
stegosaurus: A genus of large Jurassic dinosaurs remarkable for a powerful dermal armature of plates and spines.
stative: Of or pertaining to a fixed camp, or military posts or quarters. [Obs. or R.]
